notes.summary: This chapter covers the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, finding HCF and LCM by prime factorisation, and proving that numbers such as √2, √3, √5 and expressions like 5 − √3 are irrational. CBSE tests it through 1-mark MCQs and assertion-reason items on HCF, LCM and irrationals, short HCF/LCM word problems, and a 2–3 mark irrationality proof.
keyPoints: Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic: every composite number can be written as a product of primes, and this factorisation is unique apart from the order of the factors. Example: 3825 = 3² × 5² × 17.
HCF = product of the smallest power of each common prime; LCM = product of the greatest power of every prime involved. 96 = 2⁵ × 3 and 404 = 2² × 101 give HCF = 4 and LCM = 2⁵ × 3 × 101 = 9696.
For two positive integers a and b: HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b. This does not hold in general for three numbers (6, 72, 120: 6 × 360 = 2160, but the product is 51840).
Word-problem cues: 'largest / maximum / greatest number that divides' → HCF; 'smallest / least / when will they meet again' → LCM.
Remainder variants: the largest number dividing x and y leaving remainders r₁ and r₂ is HCF(x − r₁, y − r₂); the smallest number leaving remainder r when divided by a, b and c is LCM(a, b, c) + r.
A number ends in the digit 0 only if its prime factorisation contains both 2 and 5, so 6ⁿ = 2ⁿ × 3ⁿ never ends in 0.
If a prime p divides a², then p divides a — the key step in every irrationality proof.
Proof pattern for √2: assume √2 = a/b with a, b co-prime → 2b² = a² → 2 divides a → a = 2c → b² = 2c² → 2 divides b → 2 is a common factor of a and b, a contradiction.
Rational + irrational = irrational; non-zero rational × irrational = irrational (3 + √5, 2√3). But irrational × irrational can be rational: √2 × √8 = 4.
traps: Leaving a composite factor in a 'prime factorisation', e.g. writing 156 = 2² × 39 instead of 2² × 3 × 13.
Applying HCF × LCM = product of the numbers to three numbers.
Mixing up HCF and LCM in word problems, or giving the HCF itself when the question asks for the number of stacks, rows or columns.
Forgetting to subtract the remainders before taking the HCF, or forgetting to add the remainder after taking the LCM.
In irrationality proofs, not stating at the start that a and b are co-prime, so the final contradiction has nothing to contradict.
notes.examTip: Write every given number as a product of prime powers in one line first; HCF, LCM and most MCQs can then be read off in seconds.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic?
options: For positive integers a and b, there exist unique integers q and r such that a = bq + r, where 0 ≤ r < b.
Every polynomial of degree n has exactly n real zeroes.
Every prime number can be written as a sum of two composite numbers.
Every composite number can be expressed as a product of primes, and this factorisation is unique apart from the order of the factors.
questions.explanation:
The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic states that every composite number can be written as a product of primes in exactly one way, apart from the order of the factors.
Example: 156 = 2² × 3 × 13, and no other set of primes multiplies to give 156.
The statement a = bq + r is Euclid's division lemma, not this theorem.

questions.text: What is the prime factorisation of 3825?
questions.explanation:
3825 ÷ 3 = 1275; 1275 ÷ 3 = 425; 425 ÷ 5 = 85; 85 ÷ 5 = 17; and 17 is prime.
So 3825 = 3 × 3 × 5 × 5 × 17 = 3² × 5² × 17.
The options containing 51 or 85 are not prime factorisations, because 51 = 3 × 17 and 85 = 5 × 17 are composite; 3² × 5² × 19 = 4275.

questions.text: What is the HCF of the smallest prime number and the smallest composite number?
questions.explanation:
The smallest prime number is 2, and the smallest composite number is 4 = 2².
The common prime is 2, and its smallest power is 2¹.
HCF = 2.

questions.text: Using prime factorisation, what is the HCF of 96 and 404?
questions.explanation:
96 = 2⁵ × 3 and 404 = 2² × 101.
The only common prime is 2, and its smallest power is 2².
HCF = 2² = 4.

questions.text: The number 7 × 11 × 13 + 13 is:
questions.explanation:
Take 13 common: 7 × 11 × 13 + 13 = 13 × (7 × 11 + 1) = 13 × 78.
It has factors other than 1 and itself (for example 13 and 78), so it is composite.
Its value is 1014 = 2 × 3 × 13².

questions.text: The sum of a rational number and an irrational number is:
options: rational or irrational depending on the numbers
questions.explanation:
Let r be rational and s irrational, and suppose r + s = q were rational.
Then s = q − r would be a difference of two rational numbers, which is rational — a contradiction.
So the sum is always irrational (for example, 3 + √2).

questions.text: What is the LCM of 6, 72 and 120?
questions.explanation:
6 = 2 × 3, 72 = 2³ × 3² and 120 = 2³ × 3 × 5.
LCM = product of the greatest power of each prime = 2³ × 3² × 5.
= 8 × 9 × 5 = 360.

questions.text: The HCF of two numbers is 27 and their LCM is 162. If one of the numbers is 54, what is the other number?
questions.explanation:
For two positive integers, HCF × LCM = product of the numbers.
27 × 162 = 54 × (other number), i.e. 4374 = 54 × (other number).
Other number = 4374 ÷ 54 = 81.
Check: HCF(54, 81) = 27 and LCM(54, 81) = 162.

questions.text: If a = p³q² and b = pq³, where p and q are prime numbers, then LCM(a, b) is:
questions.explanation:
The LCM takes the greatest power of each prime present.
Power of p: the greater of 3 and 1 is 3. Power of q: the greater of 2 and 3 is 3.
LCM = p³q³ (while HCF = pq² and the product ab = p⁴q⁵).

questions.text: For which natural number n does 6ⁿ end with the digit 0?
questions.explanation:
A number ending in 0 is divisible by 10 = 2 × 5, so the prime 5 must appear in its prime factorisation.
6ⁿ = (2 × 3)ⁿ = 2ⁿ × 3ⁿ, whose only primes are 2 and 3.
By the uniqueness part of the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, 5 can never appear.
So 6ⁿ does not end with 0 for any natural number n.

questions.text: Three traffic lights at a junction change after every 48 seconds, 72 seconds and 108 seconds respectively. If they change together at 7:00:00 a.m., at what time will they next change together?
questions.explanation:
They next change together after LCM(48, 72, 108) seconds.
48 = 2⁴ × 3, 72 = 2³ × 3², 108 = 2² × 3³.
LCM = 2⁴ × 3³ = 16 × 27 = 432 s = 7 min 12 s.
So they next change together at 7:07:12 a.m.

questions.text: An army contingent of 616 members is to march behind an army band of 32 members in a parade. Both groups must march in the same number of columns. What is the maximum number of columns in which they can march?
questions.explanation:
The number of columns must divide both 616 and 32, and we want the largest such number, i.e. the HCF.
616 = 2³ × 7 × 11 and 32 = 2⁵.
HCF = 2³ = 8.
The maximum number of columns is 8.

questions.text: Which of the following is a rational number?
questions.explanation:
(2 − √3)(2 + √3) = 2² − (√3)² = 4 − 3 = 1, which is rational.
2 + √3 is rational + irrational, so it is irrational.
√2 × √3 = √6 is irrational.
(√2 + √3)² = 2 + 3 + 2√6 = 5 + 2√6 is irrational.

questions.text: Let p be a prime number. If p divides a², where a is a positive integer, which of the following is always true?
questions.explanation:
Write a = p₁p₂…pₙ as a product of primes; then a² = p₁²p₂²…pₙ².
If p divides a², then by the uniqueness of prime factorisation p must be one of p₁, p₂, …, pₙ.
So p divides a. Example: 3 divides 36 = 6², and 3 divides 6 (but 3² = 9 does not divide 6).
This theorem is the key step in proving that √2, √3 and √5 are irrational.

questions.text:
Assertion (A): For the numbers 6, 72 and 120, HCF × LCM is not equal to the product of the three numbers.
Reason (R): HCF(6, 72, 120) × LCM(6, 72, 120) = 6 × 360 = 2160, whereas 6 × 72 × 120 = 51840.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.explanation:
HCF(6, 72, 120) = 6 and LCM(6, 72, 120) = 360, so HCF × LCM = 2160.
Product = 6 × 72 × 120 = 51840, so R is a true statement.
Since 2160 ≠ 51840, A is true, and R is exactly the calculation that shows it.
(The rule HCF × LCM = product holds for any two positive integers, but not in general for three.)
Hence both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.text:
Assertion (A): The product of two irrational numbers is always irrational.
Reason (R): √2 and √8 are irrational numbers, but √2 × √8 = 4.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.explanation:
√2 × √8 = √16 = 4, which is rational, so R is a true statement.
This example shows that the product of two irrational numbers can be rational, so A is false.
Hence A is false, but R is true.

questions.text: To prove that √3 is irrational, we assume that √3 = a/b, where a and b are co-prime integers and b ≠ 0. Which contradiction completes the proof?
options: a and b are both even
3 divides both a and b, so a and b are not co-prime
a² = b² for all a and b
questions.explanation:
Squaring √3 = a/b gives 3b² = a², so 3 divides a², and hence 3 divides a.
Write a = 3c. Then 3b² = 9c², i.e. b² = 3c², so 3 divides b², and hence 3 divides b.
Now 3 is a common factor of a and b, which contradicts the assumption that a and b are co-prime.
So the assumption is false and √3 is irrational.

questions.text: What is the largest number that divides 70 and 125, leaving remainders 5 and 8 respectively?
questions.explanation:
Subtract the remainders: the number must divide 70 − 5 = 65 and 125 − 8 = 117 exactly.
65 = 5 × 13 and 117 = 3² × 13.
HCF(65, 117) = 13.
Check: 70 = 13 × 5 + 5 and 125 = 13 × 9 + 8.

questions.text: A sweet seller has 420 kaju barfis and 130 badam barfis. She wants to stack them so that every stack has the same number of sweets and contains only one variety, using the least area of the tray (that is, as few stacks as possible). How many stacks will there be in all?
questions.explanation:
Fewest stacks means the largest possible number of sweets per stack, which is HCF(420, 130).
420 = 2² × 3 × 5 × 7 and 130 = 2 × 5 × 13, so HCF = 2 × 5 = 10.
Stacks of kaju barfi = 420 ÷ 10 = 42; stacks of badam barfi = 130 ÷ 10 = 13.
Total number of stacks = 42 + 13 = 55.

questions.text: What is the smallest number which, when divided by 12, 16 and 24, leaves a remainder of 5 in each case?
questions.explanation:
The number minus 5 must be a common multiple of 12, 16 and 24; for the smallest number, take the LCM.
12 = 2² × 3, 16 = 2⁴, 24 = 2³ × 3, so LCM = 2⁴ × 3 = 48.
Required number = 48 + 5 = 53.
Check: 53 = 12 × 4 + 5 = 16 × 3 + 5 = 24 × 2 + 5. (101 also leaves remainder 5 but is not the smallest.)
